items.subject: hygiene
items.title: Bubbles for clean hands
items.summary: Wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry. Clean hands keep germs away!
steps: 💧 Wet your hands.
🧼 Add soap.
👏 Scrub palms, backs, fingers and thumbs. Sing a short song twice.
💦 Rinse the bubbles away.
🧻 Dry your hands.

safety.notes: Use warm, not hot, water. An adult checks the tap temperature for little ones.

basic.description: Wash at any sink or with a jug of water.

better.description: A safe step stool so a small child can reach the sink.

advanced.description: Dust hands with flour, then wash: see how scrubbing removes it all.

substitutions.use: a jug of clean water poured by a helper over a bowl
any bar soap; a small bar or soap pieces in a sock work too

items.adultNote: Model the routine before meals, after the toilet and after playing outside.

items.subject: household
items.title: Toys go home
items.summary: Every toy has a home. Let us help them get there!
steps: 👀 Look at the floor.
🧺 Pick up one toy.
🏠 Put it in its home box.
🔁 Do it again until the floor is clear.
🎉 Say "well done" to yourself!

safety.notes: Keep small parts away from babies. Lift only light things.

basic.description: One box for all the toys.

better.description: Sort toys by kind with drawn picture labels.

advanced.description: A shelf with a picture for each basket.

substitutions.use: cardboard boxes, bags or a corner of the room

items.adultNote: Sorting by colour or shape turns tidying into early maths.

items.subject: gardening
items.title: Give a plant a drink
items.summary: Plants get thirsty too. Touch the soil, then give a little drink.
steps: 👆 Touch the soil.
🏜️ Dry? The plant is thirsty.
💧 Pour a little water near the stem.
⏸️ Stop when the soil is damp, not a puddle.
☀️ Put the plant in the light.

safety.notes: Wash hands after touching soil.

basic.description: Use a cup to water any plant.

better.description: A child-sized watering can.

advanced.description: A sticker chart for watering days.

substitutions.use: a cup or a bottle with holes in the lid

items.subject: cooking
items.title: Rainbow fruit plate
items.summary: Wash fruit, peel a banana, and make a rainbow on a plate. No knife needed!
steps: 🧼 Wash your hands.
💧 Wash the fruit in water.
🍌 Peel a banana and break it into pieces.
🌈 Put red, orange, yellow and green fruit in rows.
😋 Share and eat!

hazards: choking on whole grapes or hard pieces
safety.notes: An adult cuts grapes and cherry tomatoes into quarters for young children and checks for allergies.

basic.description: Use whatever fruit is in the home.

better.description: Make a full rainbow with several colours.

advanced.description: Press soft fruit into shapes with cutters.

substitutions.use: tinned fruit (drained) or dried fruit pieces

items.adultNote: Cut round foods such as grapes lengthways into quarters for under-fives to reduce choking risk.

items.subject: electrical safety
items.title: Sockets are not toys
items.summary: Electricity is strong and can hurt. We never touch sockets or wires.
steps: 👀 Point to a socket from far away.
✋ Say: "I do not touch."
💧 Water and electricity are never friends.
🗣️ See a broken wire? Tell a grown-up straight away.

check.question: You see a wire with a broken cover. What do you do?
check.explain: Yes! Tell a grown-up and stay away.

items.adultNote: Children never open sockets, plugs or appliances. Fit socket covers only where local guidance recommends them.

items.subject: household
items.title: Set the table
items.summary: Count the people, then give each one a plate, a cup and a spoon.
steps: 🔢 Count the people who will eat.
🍽️ Put one plate for each person.
🥄 Put a spoon or fork next to each plate.
🥤 Add a cup for everyone.
😊 Call the family to eat!

safety.notes: Use unbreakable plates if possible. Adults handle sharp knives and hot dishes.

basic.description: Use what the family has.

better.description: Draw a place mat showing where things go.

advanced.description: Fold napkins and add a small decoration.

substitutions.use: a mat or cloth on the floor

items.subject: cooking
items.title: Make a sandwich
items.summary: Spread, fill and press: a sandwich is your first real meal!
steps: 🧼 Wash your hands and clean the table.
🍞 Put two slices of bread on a plate.
🧈 Spread with a blunt table knife, away from your hand.
🥒 Add a filling, like cheese, egg an adult cooked, or salad.
🔪 An adult helps you cut it in half.
🧽 Clean up and put food back in the fridge.

safety.notes: Use a blunt table knife for spreading. An adult supervises any cutting and checks allergies. Chill fillings quickly.

basic.description: One simple filling.

better.description: Add vegetables for colour and goodness.

advanced.description: Try wraps or flatbreads from different countries.

substitutions.use: flatbread, chapati, tortilla or crackers
mashed avocado, hummus or nothing

items.subject: gardening
items.title: Grow a plant in a container
items.summary: No garden? No problem. A tin, a cup or a bottle can grow a plant.
steps: 🥫 Find a clean container and make small holes in the bottom (an adult helps).
🪨 Put a few stones in the bottom, then fill with soil.
🫘 Push two or three seeds in, as deep as your fingernail.
💧 Water gently.
☀️ Put it near a window.
📅 Check every day and draw what you see.

safety.notes: Wash hands after touching soil. An adult makes the drainage holes and checks for sharp edges.

basic.description: Grow a bean from the kitchen cupboard.

better.description: Grow herbs like basil or cress from seed.

advanced.description: A window box with several plants.

substitutions.use: containers on a windowsill, balcony or doorstep
dried beans, lentils or seeds from fruit like tomatoes

items.subject: bicycle maintenance
items.title: Bike safety check: A, B, C
items.summary: Before you ride: Air in the tyres, Brakes that work, Chain that is clean.
steps: 🅰️ Air: squeeze each tyre. It should feel firm.
🅱️ Brakes: squeeze each lever and push the bike. The wheel should stop.
©️ Chain: look for rust or dirt.
🔩 Wobble the wheels: they should not be loose.
🗣️ Anything wrong? Tell an adult and do not ride.

hazards: pinched fingers in chain or spokes
safety.notes: Keep fingers away from moving chain and spokes. Do the check with the bike still or slowly pushed.

basic.description: Check by hand and eye.

better.description: Pump up soft tyres and wipe the chain.

advanced.description: Measure tyre pressure and compare with the number on the tyre side.

substitutions.use: turn the bike upside down on a soft mat, or have a helper hold it

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Where does water go?
items.summary: Clean water comes in through pipes. Used water goes out down the drain.
steps: 🚰 Turn on a tap: clean water comes from pipes under the ground.
🛁 Pull the plug: used water goes down the drain.
🔍 Look under a sink with an adult and find the bendy pipe (the trap).
🗺️ Draw a picture: street, pipe, tap, drain, sewer.

check.question: What does the bendy pipe under a sink do?
check.explain: Right! The trap keeps a little water to stop drain smells coming up.

items.subject: household
items.title: Sort and fold the laundry
items.summary: Match socks, fold shirts and help the whole family.
steps: 🧦 Find pairs of socks.
👕 Lay a shirt flat, fold in the sleeves, then fold in half.
🧺 Make a pile for each person.
📦 Put them away in drawers.

safety.notes: Children do not use the iron and keep detergents and capsules away from younger children.

basic.description: Fold by hand.

better.description: One basket per person.

advanced.description: Make a cardboard folding board for neat shirts.

substitutions.use: bags, boxes or a clean sheet

items.adultNote: Laundry capsules are a poisoning risk for young children; store them high and closed.

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Meet the pipes: plumbing parts
items.summary: Taps, pipes, traps, valves and washers: learn the names of the parts that keep water flowing.
steps: 🚰 Tap: opens and closes the water flow.
🟢 Washer or cartridge: the seal inside a tap that stops drips.
↪️ Trap: the U-shaped pipe under a sink.
🔴 Shut-off (stop) valve: turns off water to the house or one appliance.
🧪 Look under the kitchen sink with an adult and name each part you can see. Do not touch anything that is wet or near electricity.

check.question: Which part stops a tap from dripping?
check.explain: Yes. A worn washer is the most common cause of a dripping tap.

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: The plumber's toolbox
items.summary: Every job needs the right tool. Learn what plumbing tools do and which ones are for adults.
steps: 🪠 Plunger: pushes and pulls water to clear a blocked sink.
🔧 Adjustable spanner: grips nuts of different sizes.
🪣 Bucket and old towels: catch water before it spreads.
🎗️ Sealing tape: wraps threads so joints do not leak.
🔦 Torch: see into dark cupboards.
🚫 Pipe cutters, blowtorches and drain chemicals are for trained adults only.

check.question: What is the first thing to grab when a pipe drips?
check.explain: A bucket and towels stop the water spreading while you get help.

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Find the water shut-off valve
items.summary: In a leak, the shut-off valve is your best friend. Find yours with an adult.
steps: 🗣️ Ask an adult to help you look.
🔍 Look under the kitchen sink, near the water meter, or where the pipe enters the home.
🔴 It is usually a tap handle or lever on a pipe.
🔄 With the adult, learn which way closes it (often clockwise, "righty-tighty").
🏷️ Make a label: "Water shut-off".
📍 Draw a map so everyone in the home can find it.

safety.notes: An adult decides whether the valve is tested. Never force a stiff valve. Keep away from wet electrical items.

basic.description: Find it, label it and draw a map.

better.description: Fix a tag to the valve.

advanced.description: Make a home emergency card showing water, gas and electricity shut-offs (for adults to use).

substitutions.use: a strip of tape with writing on it

sources.title: WaterSense: fix a leak and save water
Home and leisure safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA)

items.adultNote: In flats and rented homes the main valve may be shared or in a communal area; ask the landlord or building manager.

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Water under the kitchen sink
items.summary: There is water leaking under the kitchen sink. What do you do?
steps: Read each situation.
Choose what you would do.
Read the feedback and think about why.

safety.notes: In real life, stay away from water near sockets or appliances and fetch an adult first.

sources.title: WaterSense: fix a leak and save water

simulation.scenario: You open the cupboard under the kitchen sink and the floor is wet. Water is dripping from a pipe.

steps.prompt: Step 1 - Remain safe. The water is spreading towards a plugged-in appliance. What first?

options.text: Keep away from the water near the appliance and call an adult.
options.feedback: Yes. Water and electricity together are dangerous. Safety first, then help.

options.text: Pull the plug out with wet hands.
options.feedback: No. Never touch plugs or switches with wet hands or while standing in water.

options.text: Ignore it and close the cupboard.
options.feedback: Leaks get worse. Telling an adult quickly saves damage.

steps.prompt: Step 2 - Identify the problem. With an adult, where do you look?

options.text: Shine a torch and dry the pipes to see where drops start.
options.feedback: Good detective work. Dry pipes make it easy to spot the drip.

options.text: Pour more water in to make it worse.

options.feedback: Look first. Is it the tap, a joint, the trap or the drain?

steps.prompt: Step 3 - Locate the shut-off. The drip is from the pipe that brings water in. What helps most?

options.text: Find the shut-off valve under the sink or the main one and let the adult close it.
options.feedback: Exactly. Turning off the water stops the leak while you decide what to do.

options.text: Hold your hand over the leak for an hour.
options.feedback: You would get tired, and it does not stop the water.

steps.prompt: Step 4 - Decide what can be attempted. The trap nut is a little loose. What could the adult try?

options.text: With the water off and a bucket under it, gently hand-tighten the nut.
options.feedback: A loose trap nut is a simple, safe fix with an adult.
Drain chemicals burn skin and eyes and do not fix leaks.

steps.prompt: Step 5 - Decide when professional help is required. The pipe is cracked and water sprays when turned on. Now what?

options.text: Keep the water off and call a qualified plumber.
options.feedback: Right. Cracked pipes, leaks near electrics, or anything you are unsure of need a professional.

options.text: Wrap it in sticky tape and forget it.
options.feedback: Tape will not hold water pressure for long. Get a plumber.

items.subject: cooking
items.title: Cook scrambled eggs
items.summary: Your first hot meal: soft, golden scrambled eggs, cooked with an adult beside you.
steps: 🧼 Wash your hands. Wash them again after cracking eggs.
🥚 Crack 2 eggs into a bowl and whisk with a fork.
🍳 With an adult, warm a pan on low heat with a little oil or butter.
↪️ Turn the pan handle inwards so nobody knocks it.
🥄 Pour in the eggs and stir slowly until there is no runny liquid left.
🔥 Turn the heat off first, then serve.

safety.notes: An adult stays beside the child at the hob. Handles turned inwards. Eggs cooked until set, with no liquid egg.

basic.description: Plain scrambled eggs.

better.description: Add chopped tomato and herbs (adult cuts).

advanced.description: Make a full breakfast plate.

substitutions.use: crumbled tofu or chickpea flour batter for an egg-free version
whatever stove or electric hot plate the family already cooks on, with the adult in charge of the heat (never a camping stove indoors)

sources.title: Food safety basics
sources.publisher: FoodSafety.gov (US Department of Health and Human Services)

items.subject: electrical safety
items.title: Five rules for electricity at home
items.summary: Electricity powers our homes. These five rules keep you safe around it.
steps: 💧 Dry hands only. Never use electrical things near water.
🔌 Pull the plug, not the cable, and only when the switch is off.
🚫 Never open sockets, plugs or appliances, or poke anything inside.
🔥 Frayed cable, burning smell, sparks or hot plug? Stop, step back, tell an adult.
🪁 Fly kites far from power lines and never climb pylons or substations.

check.question: Your phone charger cable is frayed. What should you do?
options: Tape it and keep using it
Stop using it and tell an adult
Open the plug to fix it
check.explain: Damaged cables can shock or start fires. Stop using it and tell an adult.

items.adultNote: All wiring repairs, including plugs and sockets, are for a qualified electrician.

items.subject: bicycle maintenance
items.title: Repair a bicycle puncture
items.summary: Flat tyre? Find the hole, patch it and ride again. A real repair you can be proud of.
steps: 🔄 With an adult, turn the bike over or lift it onto a stand.
🔓 Open the brake if needed and remove the wheel.
🥄 Use tyre levers to lift one side of the tyre off the rim.
🎈 Pull out the inner tube, pump a little air in and listen or feel for the hole.
💧 Can not find it? Dip the tube in a bowl of water and look for bubbles.
🔍 Check inside the tyre for the thorn or glass that caused it (feel slowly and carefully, or look).
🩹 Roughen the area, add glue if the kit needs it, wait, and press the patch on firmly.
🔁 Put the tube back, refit the tyre with your thumbs, pump to the pressure written on the tyre.
✅ Refit the wheel, close the brake and test the brakes before riding.

hazards: sharp glass or thorns in the tyre
safety.notes: An adult checks that the wheel is tight and the brakes work before anyone rides. Use glue in fresh air.

basic.description: Find the hole with water and learn the steps on a borrowed bike.

better.description: Patch the tube with a standard kit.

advanced.description: Carry a spare tube and fix flats at the roadside.

substitutions.use: the rounded handles of two old spoons (they may bend)
turn the bike upside down on a mat

sources.title: Bicycle safety
sources.publisher: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration

items.subject: sewing
items.title: Sew on a button
items.summary: A button fell off? Thread, needle and a few stitches put it back.
steps: 🪡 Cut a long arm's length of thread and push it through the needle. Tie a knot at the end.
📍 Mark where the button goes.
⬆️ Push the needle up from the back, through one hole.
⬇️ Go down through the opposite hole. Repeat 6 times.
🔁 Wind the thread around under the button 3 times to make a stalk.
🪢 Push to the back, make two small stitches and cut the thread.
📌 Put the needle back in a pin cushion.

safety.notes: An adult supervises younger learners. Keep needles in a pin cushion and away from small children.

basic.description: Practise on an old piece of fabric.

better.description: A basic sewing kit with a thimble.

advanced.description: Make a button sampler with 2-hole and 4-hole buttons.

substitutions.use: dental floss or thin wool for strong practice stitches
a bottle cap on your fingertip

sources.title: Home and leisure safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA)

items.subject: gardening
items.title: Windowsill herb garden
items.summary: Grow herbs you can smell, taste and cook with, right on a windowsill.
steps: 🥫 Collect three containers with drainage holes.
🟫 Fill with soil or compost.
🌱 Sow herb seeds such as cress, basil or coriander, or plant a cutting from a bought herb.
💧 Water when the top of the soil is dry.
📏 Measure the height every 3 days and make a chart.
✂️ Snip leaves from the top to help them grow bushy, then cook with them.

safety.notes: Wash hands and herbs before eating. Use child scissors.

basic.description: Sow seeds from coriander or mustard from the spice cupboard.

better.description: Three herbs side by side.

advanced.description: A self-watering planter to compare growth.

substitutions.use: a doorstep, balcony or any bright spot
garden soil mixed with tea leaves or coffee grounds

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Clear a slow sink with a plunger
items.summary: Sink draining slowly? A plunger and some patience usually fix it, with no chemicals.
steps: 🧤 Wear rubber gloves.
🧽 Scoop out any food or hair you can see.
💧 Leave a little water in the sink so the plunger seals.
🪠 Cover the overflow hole with a wet cloth.
⬆️⬇️ Push and pull the plunger firmly 10 to 15 times.
🚰 Run water to test. Still blocked? An adult may clean the trap over a bucket.

hazards: chemical splash-back if a drain cleaner was used earlier
safety.notes: An adult is nearby and decides if the trap is opened. Never use or mix chemical drain cleaners. If anyone has already poured a drain cleaner in, do not plunge: it can splash the chemical up; leave it to the adult. Wear gloves and wash hands after.

basic.description: Remove visible debris and flush with hot (not boiling) water.

better.description: Use a cup plunger.

advanced.description: An adult uses a hand drain snake for deeper blocks.

substitutions.use: scoop out debris and pour warm (not boiling) water; an adult may try bicarbonate of soda and vinegar, but never after any chemical drain cleaner

sources.title: Home and leisure safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA)

items.subject: electricity
items.title: How much does it cost to run?
items.summary: Use one simple formula to find out what each appliance costs: watts x hours / 1000 = kWh, then kWh x price.
steps: 🏷️ Find the power (watts, W) on each appliance label or manual. Do not open or unplug anything to look.
⏱️ Estimate the hours it is used each day.
🧮 Energy (kWh) = watts x hours / 1000.
💰 Cost = kWh x price per kWh (find the price on a family bill, or use 0.30 as an example).
📝 Example: kettle 2000 W x 0.25 h / 1000 = 0.5 kWh. 0.5 x 0.30 = 0.15 per day, about 4.50 per 30 days.
📝 Example: LED bulb 10 W x 5 h / 1000 = 0.05 kWh. 0.05 x 0.30 = 0.015 per day.
📊 Make a table for 5 appliances and find the biggest user.
💡 Suggest one change that would save energy, and work out the saving.

check.question: A 1500 W heater runs for 2 hours. How many kWh?
Electricity costs 0.30 per kWh. What do 3 kWh cost?
A 100 W TV runs 4 hours a day for 30 days. How many kWh?
check.explain: 100 x 4 / 1000 = 0.4 kWh per day, and 0.4 x 30 = 12 kWh.

items.adultNote: Share a real bill if you are comfortable so the price per kWh is local. Prices vary by country and tariff.

items.subject: cooking
items.title: Cook a pasta and vegetable meal
items.summary: Boil, chop, stir and serve: a full meal for the family.
steps: 📋 Read the recipe and get everything ready.
🧼 Wash hands and vegetables.
🔪 Chop vegetables on a board, using the claw grip (fingertips tucked in), with an adult nearby.
💧 Boil water for pasta. Lower pasta in with a spoon, not your hand.
🍅 Fry vegetables gently, add chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
🫗 An adult or you, carefully, drains the pasta away from your body.
🍽️ Mix, serve, and wash up.

safety.notes: An adult is in the kitchen. Pan handles turned inwards. Drain pasta pouring away from the body. Cool burns under cool running water and get help.

basic.description: A simple tomato pasta.

better.description: Add beans or lentils for protein.

advanced.description: Make a salad on the side and a table menu.

substitutions.use: rice, noodles, couscous or any local grain
hold the lid slightly open and pour carefully, or lift pasta out with a slotted spoon

sources.title: Food safety basics
sources.publisher: FoodSafety.gov (US Department of Health and Human Services)

items.subject: tools
items.title: Hand tools: hammer and screwdriver
items.summary: Learn to use a hammer and screwdriver safely by building a small box or shelf with an adult.
steps: 🥽 Wear safety glasses, tie back long hair, and clear the work area.
🔍 Check tools are not damaged.
🔨 Hold the hammer near the end of the handle. Start a nail with gentle taps, then move fingers away.
🪛 Choose a screwdriver that fits the screw head exactly. Turn clockwise to tighten.
🧱 Work on a stable surface, never on your lap.
🧹 Put tools away when you finish.

safety.notes: An adult stays beside the learner, checks the tools and holds or clamps the wood. No power tools without proper training. Never use tools on anything connected to electricity.

basic.description: Practise knocking nails into scrap wood.

better.description: Build a simple box from scrap wood.

advanced.description: Build a small shelf with measured cuts (adult cuts the wood).

substitutions.use: borrow a pair (they are cheap and schools or neighbours often have them); ordinary glasses and swimming goggles are not impact-proof, so without eye protection do screwdriver work only and stand well back while the adult hammers
a sturdy table protected with cardboard

sources.title: Home and leisure safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA)

items.subject: bicycle maintenance
items.title: Brakes and friction
items.summary: Brakes turn movement into heat using friction. Learn to check and adjust them with an adult.
steps: 🔍 Look at the brake pads: are the grooves still visible? Worn pads need replacing.
🎯 Pads should hit the rim (or disc) squarely, not the tyre.
✋ Squeeze the lever: it should stop well before touching the handlebar.
🔩 With an adult, turn the barrel adjuster a little to tighten a loose cable.
🧪 Test at walking speed in a safe place before any ride.
🧠 Science: more friction means more stopping force, but wet rims reduce friction, so you stop slower in rain.

safety.notes: An adult checks the brakes before the bike is ridden. If unsure, take the bike to a trained mechanic.

basic.description: Inspect pads and lever travel.

better.description: Adjust the barrel adjuster and clean the rims.

advanced.description: Fit new pads with an adult.

substitutions.use: a helper holding the bike or the bike upside down on a mat

sources.title: Bicycle safety
sources.publisher: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration

items.subject: bicycle maintenance
items.title: How bike gears work
items.summary: Count the teeth and you can work out how far one push of the pedals takes you.
steps: 🔢 Count the teeth on the front chainring (example: 40).
🔢 Count the teeth on a back sprocket (example: 20).
➗ Gear ratio = front / back = 40 / 20 = 2. The wheel turns 2 times for each pedal turn.
📏 A wheel that is 2 m around travels 2 x 2 = 4 m per pedal turn.
⛰️ Hills: a lower ratio (like 30 / 30 = 1) is easier to push but slower.
🧠 This is the same idea engineers use in cars, clocks and robots.

check.question: Front 48 teeth, back 16 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
check.explain: 48 / 16 = 3. Each pedal turn spins the wheel 3 times.

items.subject: caring for younger children
items.title: Helping care for a younger child
items.summary: Playing with, feeding and keeping a younger child safe is a big responsibility and a real skill.
steps: 📞 Always know how to reach the parent or carer and the emergency number.
👀 Keep the child in sight. Never leave a baby alone on a bed, table or in water, even for a second.
🧩 Choose toys without small parts for under-threes.
🍎 Offer only food the parent has agreed, cut small, and sit the child down to eat.
🛏️ Babies sleep on their back, in a clear cot.
😊 Be calm and kind. If the child is hurt or unwell, call the parent; in an emergency call the emergency number.

safety.notes: Teenagers help under the guidance of a responsible adult who stays reachable. A babysitting or first-aid course is strongly recommended.

basic.description: Help a parent care for a younger sibling or cousin while they are nearby.

better.description: Make an activity bag with crayons, books and safe games.

advanced.description: Take an accredited babysitting or paediatric first-aid course.

substitutions.use: a box of household items that are safe: cups, spoons, cloths, cardboard tubes

sources.title: First aid and safety
sources.publisher: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies

items.certificationNote: Knowing these steps is not a qualification. Many Red Cross and Red Crescent societies run babysitting and paediatric first-aid courses.
items.adultNote: Laws and norms on the age for babysitting differ by country; a responsible adult should always be reachable.

items.subject: sewing
items.title: Mend a tear with running and back stitch
items.summary: Do not throw it away: a few strong stitches give clothes a longer life.
steps: 🔄 Turn the item inside out and pin the edges together.
🪡 Running stitch: in and out in a straight line, small even stitches.
🔙 Back stitch: go one stitch back each time for a strong seam.
🪢 Tie off with two small stitches.
👖 Turn it back and admire your mend.

safety.notes: Keep needles and pins in a cushion and away from younger children.

basic.description: Mend a sock or a seam.

better.description: Sew a patch over a hole.

advanced.description: Decorate the mend with visible colourful stitching.

substitutions.use: fabric cut from worn-out clothes

items.subject: gardening
items.title: Grow vegetables in containers
items.summary: Lettuce, tomatoes and beans can grow in buckets and bags. Plan, plant and harvest your own food.
steps: 📅 Check what grows in your season and climate.
🪣 Choose deep containers (at least 20 cm) with drainage holes.
🟫 Fill with compost or soil mixed with compost.
🌱 Sow seeds at the depth on the packet, or plant seedlings.
💧 Water in the morning or evening. Feel the soil first.
🐌 Check for pests and pick them off by hand.
📒 Keep a diary of height, flowers and harvest weight.

safety.notes: Wash hands and vegetables. Lift with bent knees or ask for help. Children do not use garden chemicals.

basic.description: Grow from saved seeds in reused containers.

better.description: Three kinds of vegetable side by side.

advanced.description: Collect rainwater and support tall plants.

substitutions.use: buckets, sacks, crates or strong shopping bags with holes in the bottom (avoid old tyres for food plants)
home-made compost from vegetable peelings

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Fix a dripping tap
items.summary: A tap dripping once a second can waste more than a thousand litres a year. Replace the washer with an adult.
steps: 🔴 Turn off the water at the isolating valve or main shut-off. Open the tap to drain it.
🧴 Put the plug in so small parts can not fall down the drain.
🔧 Remove the handle cover and unscrew the tap head with an adjustable spanner (protect the chrome with a cloth).
🟢 Take out the old washer or cartridge and take it to match a new one.
🔁 Fit the new washer, reassemble, and turn the water back on slowly.
👀 Check for drips. Still dripping or anything cracked? Call a plumber.

safety.notes: Adult supervision required. Turn off and cool hot water first. Stop and call a qualified plumber if a valve will not close or parts break.

basic.description: Inspect and learn the parts with the water off.

better.description: Replace a rubber washer.

advanced.description: Replace a ceramic cartridge.

substitutions.use: a correctly sized spanner borrowed from a neighbour or tool library

sources.title: WaterSense: fix a leak and save water
Home and leisure safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA)

check.question: A tap drips once a second. Each drip is about 0.05 ml. How much in a day?
check.explain: 86,400 seconds x 0.05 ml = 4,320 ml, about 4.3 litres a day.

items.subject: plumbing
items.title: Hot water, pressure and becoming a plumber
items.summary: How water heaters, pressure and heating pipes work, and how people train to be plumbers.
steps: 🔥 Water heaters store hot water in a tank or heat it instantly as it flows.
📈 Pressure: water is pushed through pipes; a pressure relief valve stops a heater building too much pressure.
♨️ Central heating loops hot water through radiators and back to a boiler or heat pump.
⚠️ Gas appliances and boilers are only for registered, qualified engineers.
🎓 Plumbers learn through apprenticeships or college courses, combining classroom and on-the-job training.
📝 Research the training route for plumbers in your country.

check.question: Who should work on a gas boiler?
check.explain: Gas work is dangerous and regulated. Only qualified engineers do it.

items.subject: electrical safety
items.title: Fuses, breakers and the electrician's job
items.summary: Learn what protects a home's wiring, and why mains wiring is only for qualified electricians.
steps: 🧠 A fuse or circuit breaker cuts power if too much current flows, preventing fires.
🛡️ A residual current device (RCD or GFCI) cuts power very fast if current leaks, for example through a person.
📍 Know where the consumer unit or fuse box is so an adult can switch off power in an emergency.
🚫 Never open sockets, switches, plugs, appliances or the consumer unit, and never touch mains wiring.
🔁 If a breaker keeps tripping, there is a fault: an adult unplugs appliances and calls a qualified electrician.
🎓 Electricians train through apprenticeships and must meet national safety standards.

safety.notes: Any work on mains wiring, sockets, switches or the consumer unit is for qualified electricians only. This lesson is knowledge, not permission.

check.question: A socket has a scorch mark. What is the right action?
options: Stop using it and get a qualified electrician
check.explain: Scorch marks mean overheating. Stop using it; an electrician must inspect it.

items.certificationNote: Electrical installation work requires a qualified, and in many countries registered, electrician.
items.adultNote: Show the teen where the consumer unit is and how an adult would switch it off in an emergency; never ask them to work inside it.

items.subject: cooking
items.title: Plan and cook a week of meals
items.summary: Plan five balanced dinners on a budget, shop for them and cook at least one yourself.
steps: 🥗 Plan 5 dinners with vegetables, a protein and a grain or starch.
📝 Write a shopping list and check what is already at home.
💰 Estimate the cost and stay inside a budget agreed with your family.
🧊 Store food safely: raw meat at the bottom of the fridge, cooked food cooled and chilled within 2 hours.
🍲 Cook at least one meal start to finish, using a thermometer or checking that meat is hot all the way through.
♻️ Use leftovers for lunch the next day.

hazards: food poisoning from undercooked or badly stored food
safety.notes: An adult is in the home. Follow food safety rules for chilling, cooking and reheating.

basic.description: Plan from what the family already buys.

better.description: Shop at a local market and compare prices.

advanced.description: Batch-cook and freeze portions safely.

substitutions.use: cut into the thickest part: no pink meat and juices run clear, steaming hot

items.subject: household maintenance
items.title: Seasonal home safety check
items.summary: Small checks prevent big problems. Run a home check-up with an adult twice a year.
steps: 🔔 Press the test button on smoke alarms (and carbon monoxide alarms if fitted).
🚰 Look for drips under sinks and around the toilet.
🔌 Look for damaged cables or overloaded sockets (look only, do not open).
🪟 Check windows and doors close and lock.
🧯 Check where the fire blanket or extinguisher is, if you have one.
📝 Write a list for adults: what is fine, what needs a professional.

safety.notes: No ladder work without an adult holding it. Anything electrical or gas found faulty goes to a qualified professional.

basic.description: A walk-round with a paper checklist.

better.description: Replace alarm batteries where needed.

materials: plug-in socket tester used by an adult
advanced.description: Use simple testers with adult guidance.

substitutions.use: a list written in a notebook or on a phone
